records.what_it_measured: LatentBiopsy computes AUROC for harmful-vs-normative and harmful-vs-benign-aggressive (XSTest 'twin') discrimination via radial deviation angle from a normative-prompt principal direction, evaluated per model on 6 Qwen base/instruct/abliterated variants. Entanglement Wall computes AUROC of an activation probe on matched harmful/benign 'Twin-n163' pairs, per model, across 3-5 model families, specifically to show it is a weaker/diagnostic signal, not a ranking tool.
records.n_models_and_families: LatentBiopsy: 6 checkpoints, 2 families (Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen2.5-0.5B) x 3 variants. Entanglement Wall: 3 primary families (Llama-3.1-8B-abliterated, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Qwen2.5-7B-abliterated) plus 2 extension checkpoints (Mistral-Small-24B, Qwen2.5-32B).

used_to_rank_models.quote: both abliterated variants achieve AUROC at most 0.015 below their instruction-tuned counterparts, establishing a geometric dissociation between harmful-intent representation and the downstream generative refusal mechanism

records.prompt_budget: LatentBiopsy: 200 normative + target prompts (not few-prompt); Entanglement Wall: full Twin-n163 cohort (not few-prompt)

correlated_with_benchmark_safety.number: no correlation coefficient reported against an external benchmark; both papers report AUROC of the internal statistic itself against a held-out label, not against a behavioral benchmark score

records.verbatim_quote: Across all six variants, LatentBiopsy achieves AUROC $\geq$0.937 for harmful-vs-normative detection and AUROC = 1.000 for discriminating harmful from benign-aggressive prompts (XSTest), with sub-millisecond per-query overhead.

records.adversarial_note: Neither paper computes C12's exact ratio form (harmful-vs-twin separation RELATIVE TO harmful-vs-plain-benign separation). LatentBiopsy computes only harmful-vs-twin (XSTest benign-aggressive) AUROC per model and uses the cross-variant comparison as evidence for a different claim (geometry survives abliteration), not as a general-purpose safety ranking statistic -- borderline PUBLISHED/ADJACENT; recorded ADJACENT because the functional form (single AUROC, no plain-benign baseline ratio) differs and the paper's own framing is a mechanism claim, not a safety-ranking tool. Entanglement Wall explicitly disclaims ranking use: "At the tested read points, these activation scores behave as broad-risk detectors rather than standalone context adjudicators" -- used diagnostically only, not as a cross-model safety indicator.
records.positioning_sentence: Unlike LatentBiopsy (arXiv:2603.27412), which reports a single harmful-vs-twin AUROC per checkpoint as evidence of geometric invariance under abliteration, and Entanglement Wall (arXiv:2607.13075), which explicitly declines to use matched-pair separation as a cross-model ranking signal, our twin-discrimination statistic is defined relative to a plain-benign baseline and is validated as a safety-ranking indicator across architecture families.

records.adversarial_note: Both incumbents compute the quantity (internal score under changed presentation) per model, in a multi-model table, but explicitly frame it as a measurement-validity critique rather than a per-model safety-ranking indicator: 2608.09624's own conclusion is that 'harmfulness validation does not establish validity for success prediction' -- a critique of the metric class, not a comparison of which model is safer. Recorded ADJACENT rather than PUBLISHED because neither paper treats the per-model number as a safety comparison. No paper found that pre-signs the expected direction of the invariance gap (a negative orientation fixed before measurement) as C13 does.
records.positioning_sentence: Where Measuring the Wrong Thing (arXiv:2608.09624) uses wrapped-vs-plain AUROC reversal to argue that internal harmfulness scores are invalid outcome predictors, our presentation-invariance statistic pre-signs the expected direction and is validated as a cross-model safety-ranking feature rather than used only to critique measurement validity.

RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment

records.what_it_measured: GFS aggregates a per-layer geometric-fragility term into one scalar with a FIXED depth weight (w_l proportional to l/L, not fit by regression, no attention/MLP site decomposition). RAS squashes a window-averaged cosine-to-refusal-direction statistic through a per-family-calibrated logistic (not ridge, not depth x site features). 2502.16173 builds a 'model map' from log-likelihood vectors over a fixed text corpus (output-distribution features, not internal-activation depth x site features). PredictaBoard trains 'assessors' to predict per-instance LLM error/score but is not shown, on inspection, to use internal depth x site activation features via ridge regression.
records.n_models_and_families: GFS: 21 models, 6 alignment recipes, 3B-32B. RAS: multiple families with reference+calibration models. 2502.16173: 1,000+ language models. PredictaBoard: multiple LLM/assessor pairs (exact n not confirmed in fetched abstract).

records.prompt_budget: GFS: 500 harmful + 500 benign prompts (parent-required); RAS: requires reference model + calibration set; 2502.16173: full text corpus per model, not a small prompt set

records.adversarial_note: GFS is the structurally closest incumbent (a depth-indexed, per-model aggregated geometric score, computed and compared across 21 models) but its weight w_l is a fixed heuristic confirmed by a sensitivity appendix comparing to uniform/exponential/late-only alternatives, NOT fit by ridge or any regression, and it has no within-layer site (attention-output vs MLP-output vs residual) decomposition -- confirmed via direct fetch: 'The diagnostic operates purely at the per-layer level on residual-stream activations at the final token position. There is no mention of factoring analyses across different within-layer components or sub-sites.' RAS's calibration is a two-term fixed-weight average (w_u=w_j=0.5) plus a logistic squash with hand-set constants (c=0.75, beta=5.0), not a learned ridge coefficient vector over an explicit depth x site feature grid. 2502.16173 and weight-space/model-zoo/neural-functional-network literature predict model properties from OUTPUT-distribution or WEIGHT features across large model populations, not from internal ACTIVATION depth x site features for a safety score. No paper found fitting a ridge regression on <=24 depth-by-site activation features to build a cross-model safety metamodel after 6 general queries plus a citation-chasing hop into GFS's own weighting-scheme appendix and RAS's calibration section.
records.positioning_sentence: Unlike Skin-Deep/GFS (arXiv:2606.22676), whose depth weight is fixed at w_l proportional to l/L rather than fit, and RAS (arXiv:2606.25750), whose calibration is a fixed 0.5/0.5 average through a hand-set logistic, our ridge metamodel learns depth-by-site feature weights directly from a <=24-dimensional feature grid.

closest_prior_work.title: Diff-eRank: A Novel Rank-Based Metric for Evaluating Large Language Models
Latent Performance Profiling of Large Language Models

records.what_it_measured: Diff-eRank computes effective rank of hidden representations per model and shows it increases with model size and correlates with loss/accuracy (a CAPABILITY metric, not safety). Latent Performance Profiling (LPP) computes effective rank and participation ratio per model across 8 LLMs (0.5B-14B) as general 'latent-profile' diagnostics; a safety framing appears only as an aside ('a model with lowest entropy may be better suited for tasks requiring minimized hallucination risk'), not as the paper's safety claim. LatentBiopsy computes an angular-deviation DISPERSION statistic (sigma_theta) at a target layer, but as a per-PROMPT anomaly score within each of 6 model checkpoints, not as a per-MODEL scalar compared across models.
records.n_models_and_families: Diff-eRank: multiple LLM families/sizes (single-modal + multi-modal). LPP: 8 LLMs (LLaMA-3B/8B, Qwen-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B/14B, Mistral-7B). LatentBiopsy: 6 checkpoints, 2 families.

used_to_rank_models.quote: Intrinsic metrics including entropy, participation ratio, and effective rank clearly separate models and offer actionable guidance for selecting models based on stability, activation diversity, or representational richness

records.prompt_budget: LPP and Diff-eRank use large corpora/generation sets per model, not a 16-prompt budget

correlated_with_benchmark_safety.number: no paper found reporting a correlation between late-layer effective rank/dispersion and an external harmful-refusal or over-refusal benchmark score, across models

records.verbatim_quote: models with similar benchmark scores can exhibit contrasting latent profiles, such as differences in entropy or adaptability

records.adversarial_note: LPP is the nearest miss: it computes effective rank/participation ratio across 8 models and explicitly says these metrics 'clearly separate models,' but its use is general capability/behavioral profiling (entropy, adaptability, hallucination-risk aside), never validated against a harmful-refusal or over-refusal benchmark, and never described as a safety score. Diff-eRank likewise ties effective rank to model SIZE/capability, not safety. LatentBiopsy's dispersion statistic (sigma_theta) is the right functional family (angular/geometric dispersion) but is computed per PROMPT within a model for anomaly detection, not as a single per-model late-layer dispersion number compared across a model panel as a safety indicator. No paper found using effective rank or late-layer dispersion as a cross-model SAFETY indicator after 6 general queries plus a citation hop from LPP into its safety-adjacent aside.
records.positioning_sentence: While Latent Performance Profiling (arXiv:2605.30018) and Diff-eRank (arXiv:2401.17139) show that effective rank and participation ratio separate models on general capability, neither validates late-layer dispersion as a safety indicator against harmful-refusal or over-refusal benchmarks, which is what our metric does.

records.adversarial_note: This is an unambiguous PUBLISHED match to C16's functional form: a per-model dose-response-style slope of safety outcome vs. steering-alignment magnitude, fit independently per model and explicitly compared/ranked across 6 models by scale in a named subsection ('Effect of model scale'). The hypothesis's own prior concession that C16 has prior art is confirmed exactly by this paper, not by 2602.02132 (Joad et al.), which studies within-model steering along multiple refusal DIRECTIONS (not a magnitude dose-response slope) and is more relevant to a different candidate (direction multiplicity). Tan et al. (2407.12404) and Panickssery/Rimsky CAA (2312.06681) are the SOURCE of steering-vector methodology and generalization caveats but do not themselves report a per-model dose-response slope comparison -- they are foundational/adjacent, not the direct hit.
records.positioning_sentence: Analysing the Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors (arXiv:2603.24543) already reports self-steering dose-response slopes compared across 6 models and finds slope steepens with scale (-36.52 to -193.40); our contribution must be positioned as extending this comparison to a parent-free, few-prompt, cross-architecture-family setting rather than as introducing the slope-comparison idea itself.

AMS_2608.05578.reason: AMS's sigma statistic is a standardized (Cohen's-d-style) mean-difference of projections from 16 contrastive positive/negative prompt pairs onto a fitted direction, computed and thresholded per model -- the same 'contrastive-pair projection separation, reported per model' shape as C12's twin discrimination, though AMS's pairs are topic-contrastive rather than paraphrase-matched twins and it lacks C12's plain-benign baseline ratio.
AMS_2608.05578.statistic_quote: separation (sigma) = (mu+ - mu-) / sigma_pooled [...] confirmed identical in the public source code, src/ams/extractor.py: 'pooled_std = np.sqrt((pos_var + neg_var) / 2)'; 'separation = (pos_mean - neg_mean) / pooled_std'

N-GLARE_2511.14195.reason: N-GLARE's JR Min/Max is a stability RATIO of a Jensen-Shannon-divergence trajectory statistic taken across four different probing conditions (Benign, Jailbreak, Ideal Refusal, Plain Query) and across trajectory slices -- structurally an invariance-across-presentations ratio, the same shape as C13, though N-GLARE's four conditions are probe-content types rather than surface-presentation variants of the same content.

RAS_2606.25750.reason: RAS is the incumbent whose ROLE is closest to a metamodel: it maps several internal cosine-to-refusal-direction statistics (UnsafeScore, JailbreakScore) through fixed weights and a calibrated logistic into one 0-100 per-model safety score -- the same 'combine several internal features into one calibrated cross-model score' shape as C14's ridge metamodel, though RAS uses a hand-set 0.5/0.5 average and logistic squash rather than a fitted ridge regression over an explicit depth-by-site feature grid.
RAS_2606.25750.statistic_quote: s(M) = w_u*UnsafeScore + w_j*JailbreakScore with w_u=w_j=0.5 [...] RAS(M) = 100/(1 + exp(β(d_aligned − c))) [...] with c = 0.75 and β = 5.0

LatentBiopsy_2603.27412.reason: LatentBiopsy's core statistic is an angular-deviation DISPERSION (sigma_theta of the radial angle from a fitted normative direction, fit at a chosen target layer), the same 'geometric dispersion of late-representation activations' shape as C15, even though LatentBiopsy reports it as a per-prompt anomaly score within a model rather than a single per-model scalar compared across a model panel.
LatentBiopsy_2603.27412.statistic_quote: harmful prompts exhibit a near-degenerate angular distribution (\sigma_\theta \approx 0.03 rad), an order of magnitude tighter than the normative distribution (\sigma_\theta \approx 0.27 rad), preserved across all alignment stages including abliteration
